chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah, Exalted is He, support him—informed me of, through the preceding chain of transmission, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked Abā 'Abdillāh عليه السلام about a mouse that falls into the well, or a bird.

He عليه السلام said: “If you reach it before it becomes putrid, draw out seven buckets from it. If it is a cat or something larger than it, draw out thirty buckets or forty buckets from it. And if it has become putrid such that the smell of putrefaction is found in the water, then draw out the well until the putrid smell departs from the water.”

And no one has the right to say: How did you act upon forty buckets regarding the cat, the dog, and what resembles them, and upon seven buckets regarding the hen and the bird, when in these two reports there is no definitive specification of forty buckets, but rather they only indicate it by way of choice? Why did you not act on reports other than these two that indicate a lesser amount than what you have adopted? Because when we act upon what we have mentioned—drawing forty buckets for what a dog and the like has fallen into, and drawing seven buckets for what a hen and the like has fallen into—then there is no disagreement among our companions regarding the permissibility of using what remains of the water. Also, the reports that indicate less than that are included within this. But if we act upon other than that, we would be rejecting these two reports altogether and turning to that concerning which there is disagreement. For that reason, we acted upon the furthest extent of what the reports have stated, as opposed to what has come in reports that indicate less than what we have mentioned regarding the number of buckets to be drawn.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ دَلْوًا: forty buckets, the higher juristic amount adopted in certain cases
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being assessed for taharah (ritual purity)
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse that falls into the well
key_terms.رِيحُ النَّتْنِ: the smell of putrefaction found in the water
key_terms.سَبْعَ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets to be drawn in the specified case
key_terms.عِدَّةِ النَّزْحِ: the number of buckets to be drawn out
key_terms.نَزَحْتَ: you draw out water from the well

ai.seo_question: How many buckets must be drawn from a well if a mouse, bird, cat, or dog falls into it according to Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on purifying well water when a mouse, bird, cat, dog, or similar animal falls into it, specifying different amounts of water to be drawn depending on the case and whether the water has become putrid. The closing passage explains a juristic method of preferring the maximum reported amount in order to ensure permissibility and avoid acting on disputed positions.
